content.text:
When a hold expires, the next waiting member for that item now gets it. All 60 tests pass: the 59 existing ones plus one new one.

**The change.** In `lib/holds/pickup-shelf.js`, `expireUncollectedHolds` now calls `fulfilNextHold` once per affected item, after it has expired all the stale holds. The next waiting hold becomes `ready` with `readyOn` set to `today`. I took "the day the expired hold was cleared" to mean the day the expiry runs. `pickupDeadline` therefore counts the new member's ten days from that day. The function still returns only the expired holds.

**The test.** The new test in `test/holds.test.js` expires one ready hold with two members queued behind it. It checks that the first one becomes ready from `TODAY` and the second stays waiting.

I made no changes to any of the existing tests.

- **No notice is sent.** `returnItem` returns a hold-ready notice for the member who gets the item. I couldn't do the same here without changing the return value that the existing test checks. Nothing calls `expireUncollectedHolds` outside the tests yet, so the promoted member isn't told. Whoever wires up the expiry job will need to send that notice. Do you want me to extend the return value for this?
- **A ready hold elsewhere doesn't block it.** If another ready hold for the same item is still on the shelf, a waiting member still gets promoted. An item has one barcode, so that shouldn't happen in real data.
